title: A loop stalled on sign-in tells the person again when they come back to the Mac
goal: When the loop cannot sign in it says so once, at the moment it stalls, and then once a day. On 2026-09-30 that one notice went out at 10pm, nobody was at the Mac, and the loop sat idle for about twenty hours until the person happened to sign in again the next evening. It should also tell them the first time they come back to the Mac while it is still stalled.
notes: Evidence: queue/loop.log shows sign-in failures from 2026-09-30 22:05 to 2026-10-01 18:25 local (39 attempts); queue/history.jsonl has a single stall_notified event at 2026-10-01T05:05:09Z (hours 0). notify_person and the once-a-day rule are in queue/bin/go-loop.sh; person-at-mac.sh reads HIDIdleTime. loop-day.mjs for that day: tasks 10.8 per cent, between 74.9 per cent.
acceptance: While the loop is stalled on sign-in or the spend limit, the first time the person returns to the Mac after being away (the same idle reading the walks use) they get one notice naming the action that ends the stall
At most one such notice per return, and none once the stall has cleared
A drill shows it: a stalled loop, the person away then back, exactly one notice; the person back with no stall, none
The dashboard and loop.log say when the return notice went out
